newsitem.title: POLAND: Czech, Polish shares defy E.European bearish mood.
newsitem.headline: Czech, Polish shares defy E.European bearish mood.

text.p: The Prague bourse, buoyed by the right's strong showing in the first round of Senate elections, led other East European exchanges this week, with most markets seeing light trading volumes and subdued buying interest.
Warsaw shares inched up slightly amid a general sideways trend while all other exchanges saw losses.
The CESI Central European Share Index closed at 1,402.89 points on Thursday, up 51.19 points or 3.79 percent.
PRAGUE

Czech shares rallied for four straight sessions on the back of strong results by Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's conservative Civic Democratic Party (ODS) in the first round of Senate elections last weekend.
Major issues led the way after a series of losing sessions saw the PX50 fell 17 percent of its value since September 5.
Dealers were reluctant to predict a sustained bull run on the basis of one week's results and warned investors to wait for the second round of voting this weekend.
"This was just the first round and (the vote) isn't won yet," said Jan Sykora of Wood & Company in Prague.
SPT Telecom was the top gainer among blue chips, rising 217 points, or eight percent, to 2,972.
WARSAW
Polish shares inched up this week and analysts said the market should rise slightly on Friday but would maintain its horizontal trend into next week.
Analysts said demand on Friday could be buoyed by the lower house of parliament's (the Sejm's) passing of less-inflationary 1997 tax legislation on Thursay.
"We might have a rise to one percentage point, but the decision's effect might only last until Friday," said Wojciech Smolka, an analyst at Bank Slaski brokerage.
The Sejm's previous tax bill before a Senate amendment offered a steep tax cut for low earners.
The main market's all-share WIG index closed at 13,628.4 points on Thursday, up 65.7 points or 0.5 percent from last Friday's close.
BUDAPEST
Hungarian share prices fell on profit-taking early in the week but then edged up, lifted by strong gains by Richter drug maker and oil and gas company MOL.
Traders said Richter and another drug maker, Egis, have been undervalued in recent weeks and their gains this week did not surprise as western investors were interested in the low prices.
Traders saw further downward corrections after the bourse's strong showing for most of the year.
BRATISLAVA
The Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) saw another week of listless trade and the 12-share SAX index fell 11.49 points to 179.14 on Thursday from Monday's opening at 190.63.
Brokers saw no revival in the near future.
BUCHAREST
Thin demand kept volumes light on the Bucharest bourse this week with buying interest centred on fertiliser maker Azomures SA and engineering company Artrom SA.
Two independent indices showed little movement with VAB slightly down and BIG just up over the week.
ZAGREB
Croatian stocks took a further dive on Thursday after trading lower for most of the week. No recovery was seen as large investors held back.
Traders said a recent government announcement to scrap some 9,000 employee buyout contracts was scaring investors away.
Only fully-listed drugs firm Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka bucked the bearish trend, analysts said.
LJUBLJANA
Slovenian shares slipped this week in total turnover of 603.8 million tolars ($4.4 million).
Preferred shares of Dolenjska bank were the leading decliners, falling 10.5 percent, while the biggest gainer was brokerage Dadas, rising 16 percent.
TIRANA
On Tirana's Stock Exchange 100 million leks ($980,400) worth of T-bills changed hands this week.
